subsystems.name: Drilling and well construction
subsystems.role: creates deep boreholes to reach hot rock.

subsystems.name: Stimulated reservoir
subsystems.role: the underground heat exchanger — a network of opened fractures.

subsystems.name: Circulation system
subsystems.role: moves water from injection wells, through the hot rock, to production wells.

subsystems.name: Power plant
subsystems.role: converts the produced heat into electricity.
parts: organic Rankine cycle turbine or flash turbine

subsystems.name: Monitoring and control
subsystems.role: tracks reservoir performance and manages induced seismicity.

buildSteps.title: Explore and select site
buildSteps.detail: Geological mapping, temperature-gradient wells and seismic surveys locate hot rock at drillable depths, typically 3–10 km.

buildSteps.title: Drill injection well
buildSteps.detail: Rotary drilling with hardened bits, often directional, reaches the target formation; steel casing is cemented in place.

buildSteps.title: Stimulate the reservoir
buildSteps.detail: Water is injected at high pressure to open existing fractures and create a connected network. Proppant may be added to hold fractures open.

buildSteps.title: Drill production well
buildSteps.detail: A second well (or several) is drilled to intersect the stimulated fracture network, completing the loop.

buildSteps.title: Test circulation
buildSteps.detail: Water is pumped from injection to production well while flow rate, temperature and pressure are measured to confirm the reservoir works as a heat exchanger.

buildSteps.title: Build power plant
buildSteps.detail: A binary-cycle plant (using a working fluid with a low boiling point) or a flash plant is constructed at the surface.

buildSteps.title: Connect and commission
buildSteps.detail: Wells are linked to the power plant, circulation begins, and electricity generation is ramped up.

buildSteps.title: Operate and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Water circulates continuously; electricity is generated; seismicity and reservoir pressure are monitored and managed.

prerequisites.why: oil and gas drilling is mature, but crystalline rock at high temperatures wears out bits and tools quickly.
used in oil and gas, but creating large, connected, long-lived reservoirs in hot dry rock is still being optimised.
electronics and seals degrade above about 200 °C, limiting measurement and control at depth.
widely used in conventional geothermal fields to generate electricity from moderate-temperature fluids.
injecting water can trigger small earthquakes; monitoring and mitigation protocols are still developing.

pathway.milestone: research projects such as Utah FORGE demonstrate multi-well circulation and heat extraction
pathway.unlocks: proof that engineered reservoirs can sustain flow.

pathway.milestone: first commercial EGS plants of tens of megawatts in favourable locations
scaling to hundreds of megawatts and drilling cost reductions
pathway.unlocks: geothermal power in regions without natural hot springs.

pathway.milestone: widespread deployment using advances from oil and gas drilling
pathway.unlocks: firm, low-carbon baseload power across many countries.
